All 7 Chakras Explained: Functions, Blockages & Healing Practices

Walk through all 7 chakras with their function, common signs of blockage, and a traditional healing practice for each — Root through Crown.

Key Takeaways

  • •Each of the 7 chakras governs a distinct life function, from safety and belonging (Root) to unity and wisdom (Crown).
  • •A "blocked" chakra shows up as a recurring pattern — over- or under-expression of its theme — not a single event or diagnosis.
  • •Traditional practices for each chakra include specific breathwork, postures, mantras and stones, matched to its theme.
  • •This is a complementary wellness framework, not a medical or diagnostic system — persistent symptoms need a qualified professional.
Parikshiva Published July 28, 2026 2 min read

  • 1. Root (Muladhara) — Safety and Belonging
  • 2. Sacral (Svadhisthana) — Creativity and Pleasure

  • 7. Crown (Sahasrara) — Unity and Wisdom

This guide walks through all 7 chakras together — what each one governs, the pattern that traditionally signals it feels blocked, and one accessible healing practice to pair with it. If you want the foundational overview first, start with the beginner's guide.

1. Root (Muladhara) — Safety and Belonging

Function: grounding, physical safety, financial and material stability. Sign of blockage: chronic restlessness, anxiety about survival or money, feeling perpetually unsettled. Healing practice: slow, grounding breathwork, walking barefoot, and postures like Mountain Pose that emphasise a stable base.

2. Sacral (Svadhisthana) — Creativity and Pleasure

Function: creativity, emotional flow, sensuality and adaptability. Sign of blockage: creative blocks, emotional numbness, or swinging into excess. Healing practice: gentle hip-opening postures, free-form movement, and journaling to reconnect with emotion.

3. Solar Plexus (Manipura) — Willpower and Confidence

Function: personal power, confidence, decisiveness. Sign of blockage: chronic self-doubt, or overcompensating with control and domination. Healing practice: core-strengthening postures, breath-of-fire pranayama, and small acts of decisive follow-through.

4. Heart (Anahata) — Love and Connection

Function: compassion, connection, the bridge between the more physical lower chakras and the more subtle upper ones. Sign of blockage: difficulty trusting others, or over-giving at your own expense. Healing practice: chest-opening postures, loving-kindness meditation, and rose quartz as a traditional focal stone.

5. Throat (Vishuddha) — Expression and Truth

Function: authentic communication, honest expression, listening. Sign of blockage: difficulty speaking up, or talking over others without listening. Healing practice: humming or chanting the seed sound HAM, gentle neck stretches, and journaling unspoken thoughts.

6. Third Eye (Ajna) — Intuition and Insight

Function: intuition, clarity, seeing beyond the immediate and literal. Sign of blockage: confusion, overthinking, or dismissing your own instincts. Healing practice: seated meditation with a focus between the eyebrows, and reducing sensory overload before sleep.

7. Crown (Sahasrara) — Unity and Wisdom

Function: a felt sense of connection to something larger than the individual self. Sign of blockage: rigid cynicism, or feeling disconnected from meaning and purpose. Healing practice: silent meditation, time in nature, and simply sitting with stillness without an agenda.

A complementary practice, not medical or mental health care

These are traditional, symbolic practices for reflection — none of them diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any physical or mental health condition. If a pattern feels persistent or serious, please see a qualified medical doctor or licensed mental health professional; chakra work can sit alongside good care, never replace it.
